# Assumption ledger — Gosling shared shell productization

Assumptions are conservative defaults, not verified facts. Each must be confirmed, superseded, or carried visibly into final handoff.

| ID | Assumption | Basis at planning time | Risk if wrong | Confirmation method / gate | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SHP-ASM-001 | Each shell bundles the exact Gosling binary it was tested with; external installed-core discovery is out of scope | Safest compatibility model and current Electron package embeds `gosling` | External-core support would add discovery, trust, version, and lifecycle complexity | ADR-0008 operator/design review, Gate 2 | proposed |
| SHP-ASM-002 | Product profiles can be JSON and parsed with the existing Node/TypeScript stack without a new dependency | Forge and build scripts already run in Node; JSON is deterministic | Existing repo convention or ergonomics may require another format | Inspect build tooling and record ADR-0007, Gate 2 | confirmed by dependency-free Gate 3 resolver |
| SHP-ASM-003 | Product profile is source-controlled build input, not user-editable runtime settings | Agreed packaging/release role and authority boundary | Runtime editing would require migration, persistence, trust, and UX contracts | ADR-0007 and profile entrypoint inspection, Gate 2 | accepted/binding by ADR-0007 |
| SHP-ASM-004 | A dedicated shell main/preload/renderer Vite entry can coexist in `ui/desktop` without a new workspace package | Existing `plugin-vite` setup and shared code location | Forge/Vite may make product selection brittle or enlarge default bundle | Prototype entry build and package, Gates 3–4 | design accepted; runtime build still to validate |
| SHP-ASM-005 | `createMinimalShellHost` plus existing `goslingServe` lifecycle is the correct process owner and should be extended rather than copied | PR #46 architecture and existing cleanup/readiness behavior | Missing events/ownership could require a focused host contract change | Failure-path integration tests, Gate 4 | to validate |
| SHP-ASM-006 | Shell preload should be narrower than full Desktop preload, even if that requires a separate entry file | Gate 2 confirmed full preload exposes broad file/settings/updater operations | Some shared renderer component may depend on broad APIs | ADR-0008 and IPC negative-space tests, Gates 2/4 | accepted/binding by ADR-0008 |
| SHP-ASM-007 | Shared protected credential/config authority remains intentionally common while app userData/cache/logs/runtime state are product-isolated | Merged shell architecture | Electron `userData` isolation could accidentally isolate intended config if backend paths derive from it | Explicit path matrix and coexistence tests, Gates 2/3/6 | to validate |
| SHP-ASM-008 | Two neutral fixture identities are sufficient to prove collision/isolation machinery without implementing domain shells | Need at least two consumers/identities for isolation | Real products may expose unmodeled platform metadata needs | Domain-team review after shared acceptance; Gate 8 handoff | implemented for profile/identity fixtures; package proof pending |
| SHP-ASM-009 | At least one local/CI platform can launch a packaged Electron fixture headlessly or through existing automation | Existing Electron/Playwright infrastructure and release quick tests | No environment may support installed GUI launch reliably | Gate 0 harness inventory and Gate 6 spike | to validate |
| SHP-ASM-010 | Other platform jobs can provide structural/readback proof when full installed GUI automation is unavailable | Cross-platform CI limitations are common | Structural proof alone misses runtime defects | Explicit per-target acceptance and unverified status, Gates 6–8 | proposed |
| SHP-ASM-011 | Shell compatibility information can be derived from existing initialization/provisioning responses or added additively to canonical Rust DTOs | Shell identity/schema versions already exist | Required method/core revision metadata may be absent | Contract inspection and ADR-0008, Gate 2 | partially confirmed: custom-method capability metadata is absent and must be exposed canonically in Gate 4 |
| SHP-ASM-012 | Exact core pinning is acceptable for first release; semver ranges remain unsupported until tested | Production-safe initial policy | Release cadence/storage may require independent core updates | ADR-0008 and compatibility tests, Gates 2/4 | accepted for initial release |
| SHP-ASM-013 | Existing diagnostic/startup services can be composed into shell diagnostics rather than duplicated | `startupDiagnostics` and `goslingServe` already record bounded startup state | They may contain Desktop-specific fields or insufficient redaction | Field inventory/sentinel tests, Gate 4 | to validate |
| SHP-ASM-014 | Full Gosling handoff can use a profile-specific protocol or approved canonical `gosling://` destination without creating a new external IPC service | Existing deep-link handling and handoff envelope | OS ownership/argument semantics may differ by platform | Deep-link/protocol tests and ADR-0008, Gates 2/6 | to validate |
| SHP-ASM-015 | Shell product assets can live in repository-relative profile roots and be validated before Forge | Existing icons/resources are source-controlled | External/private branding pipelines may provide assets later | ADR-0009; maintain adapter seam, Gate 2/7 | confirmed by approved-root target asset validation |
| SHP-ASM-016 | Release jobs can reuse current platform workflows internally instead of duplicating them | Current workflows already package Gosling on major targets | Existing workflows may be too Gosling-specific or have incompatible inputs | Workflow module map and dry-run prototype, Gate 7 | to validate |
| SHP-ASM-017 | A real shell release remains in the Gosling repository/release authority initially | Current Forge publisher/release workflows target Gosling | Products may need separate repositories/feeds/permissions | Operator decision before any production profile; SHP-REQ-032 remains P2 | unresolved |
| SHP-ASM-018 | Fixture and unsigned builds must always have updater disabled and cannot be promoted by workflow inputs | Safety requirement from agreed plan | None; weakening creates accidental publication risk | Hard-coded validation and workflow negative tests, Gates 3/7 | confirmed in profile/Forge adapter; workflow proof pending |
| SHP-ASM-019 | `scripts/with-rusty-v8-cache.sh` is the intended canonical V8 archive mechanism; CI omission is the integration defect | Script implements verified download/cache/locking; Gate 0 confirmed wrapper/build-script contract and isolated cold/warm seed path | Linux download path could still expose a target-specific helper defect | Regression suite plus fresh Linux CI, Gate 1 | confirmed for integration design; Linux runtime evidence pending |
| SHP-ASM-020 | Trusted upstream V8 assets and immutable checksums exist for every initially required Linux target/profile | Helper contains checksums for 145.0.0 targets at planning time | Missing exact checksum blocks clean CI | Exercise Linux download and compare upstream immutable asset metadata, Gate 1 | x86_64 Linux release confirmed by real download/checksum/archive; aarch64 Linux/runtime CI remains unverified |
| SHP-ASM-021 | No live provider credential is needed to prove shell host/runtime provisioning and policy | Existing runtime E2E uses deterministic/local paths | Session creation might require configured model/provider in packaged fixture | Design fixture provider/model path, Gate 2/4 | to validate |
| SHP-ASM-022 | Profile collision checks can enumerate all source-controlled production/fixture profiles | Planned central profile root | External profiles could evade static collision checking | Define approved roots and release-time fleet input, Gate 2/3 | confirmed for source-controlled approved roots |
| SHP-ASM-023 | Default Gosling packaging must remain byte/field-equivalent when no shell profile is supplied except intentional refactoring output | Backward compatibility requirement | Productization could regress full Desktop packages | Golden/readback comparison, Gate 3/7 | confirmed by default Forge configuration regression |
| SHP-ASM-024 | Existing GitHub Actions permissions/environment controls can express required signing and human approval gates | Current release workflows already use environments/secrets | Repository settings may be absent or differ | Workflow readback/manual maintainer gate, Gate 7 | to validate |
| SHP-ASM-025 | No repository-specific test ledger exists at planning baseline | `docs/testing/test-ledger.yaml` was absent during orientation | A later ledger/convention could require updates | Recheck AGENTS/docs before every test-changing gate | rechecked at Gate 3; still absent |
| SHP-ASM-026 | The current completed Desktop-workspaces `docs/build/*` artifacts should not be overwritten by this new campaign | Existing artifacts are campaign-specific and complete | Mixing status would erase historical truth | Namespaced `docs/build/shell-productization/` package | accepted |
| SHP-ASM-027 | The neutral fixture renderer may include test probe controls but those controls must be absent from publishable builds | Needed for packaged acceptance without domain behavior | Probe controls could leak into release artifacts | Compile-time fixture entry and package negative tests, Gate 5/6 | proposed |
| SHP-ASM-028 | Cross-platform package identity can be normalized and validated before OS packaging with target-specific readback as final authority | Standard packaging pattern | Platform tooling may transform names unexpectedly | Package verifier on each target, Gate 7 | partially confirmed by validators; package readback pending |

## Review policy

- `binding` assumptions are treated as requirements unless amended by operator-approved plan change.
- `unresolved` assumptions block any dependent production/release decision but need not block fixture implementation.
- Gate 8 handoff lists every assumption not confirmed by observed evidence.
